name: Aishwarya Dongre
bio: An Indian Police Service Officer. She holds domain specific expertise on Combatting cyber crimes against women and children. Ms. Dongre is part of the INTERPOL South Asian Child Trafficking Victim Identification Task Force and was an integral part of the Kerala Police team addressing child sexual abuse. She had the privilege of representing Kerala Police at the National security conference 2023 of the Government of India on Kerala Police’s institutionalized approach in Combating Online Child sexual abuse. She has been accoladed for her sessions for police recruit trainees on Child Sexual Abuse material and police-public perception at Kerala police academy. Ms Aishwarya has authored a research paper : The Perfect Victim- which analyses crime data trends between online and offline child sexual abuse and another research based on Drug Investigation in India. She organized a “Women Security Fair – Uyare,” a one of its kind gathering of district departments to provide a multi-pronged approach to women’s safety and security. Over 3000 women attended the initiative, where attendees discussed cyber security, financial security, employment security, and health and emotional well-being. Ms Dongre set up Kerala’s first Cyber Simulator room in Kochi for protecting children in the online space by exposing them experientially to online cyber crimes. She also Initiated A Cyber Ambassador Project as a District Police head of Thrissur Rural, that made youth leaders as cyber safety ambassadors from different colleges and youth organizations. She believes that technology is here to grow – and as enforcement officers riding the tide is the only way forward. She was one of the 5 participants chosen from India for the prestigious US Department of State’s International Visitor Leadership Program in 2024 on working in the space of Combating Human Trafficking with Technology.

name: Akash Pugalia
bio:
Akash Pugalia is Chief Digital Officer at TP, where he leads TP.ai Data Services and the company's global Trust & Safety business. With more than 25 years of experience across technology-enabled services, Media & Entertainment, Gaming and Trust & Safety, Akash has built and led global businesses serving some of the world's leading technology platforms.

His work focuses on the intersection of AI, data, human expertise and trust, with particular emphasis on responsible AI, AI data, online safety and the evolving role of human intelligence in AI-enabled environments. He is passionate about building practical approaches to Trust & Safety that balance innovation, scale and the need to protect people in increasingly complex digital ecosystems.

name: Ankit Bose
bio:
Ankit Bose leads the AI vertical at Nasscom with a clear conviction that 'AI must scale with trust, not hype'. He works at the intersection of policy, innovation, startups, research, and enterprise adoption, thereby helping organizations move from pilots to production-grade AI that businesses can run and engineers can implement. His mission is to turn India’s diversity and scale into a global advantage, shaping the 'Safe, Trusted, and Scalable AI' and unlocking a $500B opportunity through execution.
 
As head of Nasscom AI, Ankit architects ecosystem programs like the Nasscom GenAI Foundry to connect deep-tech startups with enterprise demand, leads the Nasscom Responsible AI practices around safety and accountability, and guides CXOs through adoption frameworks and maturity benchmarks.

name: Ashwini Natesan
bio:
Ashwini Natesan is a legal consultant and research fellow specializing in Technology, Media & Telecommunications (TMT) law.  As a Research Fellow at LIRNEasia, a tech policy think tank, founded in Sri Lanka, she focuses on issues relating to data protection, data governance, online safety, AI ethics, and the use of data for public good.  She is also a Consultant at Julius & Creasy for TMT law. Additionally, she undertakes independent projects related to online safety, data protection, AI governance, and the right to information. She has several publications to her credit and frequently presents at conferences nationally and internationally.


She is a Director on the Board of a leading financial institution in Sri Lanka. Previously, she was part of the Responsible AI sub-committee tasked with drafting Sri Lanka's National AI Strategy. She is a part of the Digital Trust Alliance Board, an initiative to promote trust and safety. 


She was selected to the Media Policy Institute at the University of Oxford in 2024 and is a former Fellow of the Internet Law and Policy Foundry. She was also selected as a regional expert for the Asia Pacific Consultation on Human Rights in the Digital Space by the International Commission of Jurists in 2025. She holds an LL.M. (Master of Laws) from the National University of Singapore and has completed various certifications, fellowships, and programmes, including in AI policy, AI Governance, and AI Safety Fundamentals.

name: Bansuri Swaraj
bio: Bansuri Swaraj is an Indian lawyer and politician currently serving as Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) for New Delhi. She earned her BA in English Literature from the University of Warwick, studied law at BPP Law School and qualified as a Barrister from the Inner Temple, completing a Master of Studies at Oxford University.

name: Barkha Dutt
designation: Award-winning TV journalist, anchor and columnist
bio: Barkha Dutt is one of India's best known broadcast journalists. With close to 30 years of reporting experience Barkha shot to fame with her frontline reporting of the Kargil war in 1999. After two decades with NDTV she left to start her own company, digital platform Mojo Story. She is the winner of more than 60 national and international awards including India's fourth highest civilian honour, the Padmashri. She has also been recognised as a Global Leader for Tomorrow by the World Economic Forum. Barkha Dutt is a columnist with the Washington Post, Hindustan Times, The Week, and Dainik Bhaskar.

name: Basarbatu Can
bio: Basarbatu (Basar) Can is a Machine Learning Scientist at Booking.com, where he works on applying large language models to Trust & Safety-related business cases. He has approximately 15 years of experience spanning machine learning, software engineering, bioinformatics, optics, and sensor technology. His career includes senior data science roles at ABN AMRO and GE Power, as well as earlier engineering and research positions at GE Aviation, Ford, and academic and technology organizations in Turkey. His experience spans financial services, energy, aerospace, automotive, biotechnology, and applied research. Basarbatu holds a PhD in Machine Learning from Sabancı University, an MSc in Optics from Koç University, and a BSc in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from Bilkent University. His academic work includes online anomaly detection, Neyman–Pearson classification, active learning, bioinformatics, MEMS, and computational optics. He has authored more than 10 research publications and holds more than two patents.

name: Caroline Humer
bio:
Caroline Humer began her career in child protection, specializing in the global response to child sexual exploitation and missing children. Over nearly two decades, she has worked at the intersection of technology, protection, and international collaboration, helping shape new approaches to some of the most complex challenges facing vulnerable people online.
 
In 2022, Caroline co-founded the Trust & Safety Forum in Lille, France, creating a dedicated space for the rapidly growing Trust & Safety community to connect, exchange expertise, and develop practical solutions for a safer digital environment. Building on its success, she co-founded the Trust & Safety Festival in 2024, expanding the conversation internationally and bringing together platforms, regulators, policymakers, law enforcement, NGOs, researchers, technology providers, and other stakeholders committed to making the digital world safer for everyone.
 
In 2024, Caroline also co-founded Survivors & Technology Solving Image-Based Sexual Abuse (STISA), a global NGO focused on transforming the response to image-based sexual abuse. STISA works to equip survivor support helplines with the technology, resources, and connections they need to help survivors secure the removal of non-consensual intimate images and prevent further revictimization.

name: Caroline Simangaliso Makumbe
bio: Caroline Makumbe is a Child-centred design expert with over 23 years’ experience working at the intersection of children, technology and digital policy. Her work at Kutunga Design Academy & Innovation Lab advances safety-by-design approaches that put children at the centre of technology and innovation. Her work is deeply motivated by raising Gen Alpha children. She is committed to helping build digital experiences where children are safe, heard and able to thrive.

name: Divya Chandra
bio:
Divya Chandra is Chief Programme Officer at BOOM, specialising in trust & safety, digital literacy and AI ethics. She has actively conducted AI literacy, verification, and media literacy training sessions for journalists, election management bodies, teenagers, journalism students, engineering students and the general public—in India and South Asia.

She has collaborated on initiatives with Google, YouTube, UNICEF, International Centre for Journalists (ICFJ), IIIDEM under Election Commission of India, CUTS & US Consulate General Kolkata, Journalists' Association of Bhutan, IIT Madras, OP Jindal Global University, Azim Premji University, Shiv Nadar University, among others. She is a core member of the Teen Fact-Checking Network India and the North East Facts Network. 

Previously, she worked as Correspondent-Fact Check at The Quint, where she investigated online mis/disinformation and delved deeper into the psychology of misinformation.

name: Dr Abigail Bentley
bio: Dr Abigail Bentley is an independent researcher and social scientist specialising in violence, trauma, and mental health. She has held academic positions at University College London, the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine and the University of Valencia. She was lead researcher and author of Chayn's 'Not Just Nudes' study, investigating image-based abuse in Pakistan and its diaspora. She has led research and evaluation across academia and civil society, including with Chayn, the UK Department for Education, the UK Youth Endowment Fund, and Save the Children, alongside sustained work with specialist organisations addressing violence and abuse, particularly within South Asian communities.

name: Dr Priyanka Bhalla
designation: Director of Public Policy, Government and Global Impact, APAC
bio: Dr Priyanka Bhalla is the APAC Director for Public Policy, Government and Global Impact, and leads programs and partnerships work for the region. She has over twenty years of experience in the international development and tech policy space, including with the United Nations, International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent, Quilt.AI, and Meta. She holds a BA in Cultural Anthropology and French, a Master’s in International Affairs, and a PhD in Public Policy, with a focus on both offline and online child and women’s protection issues.

name: Dr. Ranjana Kumari
bio: Dr. Ranjana Kumari has been a leading advocate for women’s rights in India for over four decades, combining activism, scholarship, and policy engagement. She has advised the Government of India through roles on the National Commission for Women, Ministry of Women and Child Development, NHRC, and Ministry of Labour, and has served as a Gender Expert at the ILO and United Nations in Geneva. Recognized with national and international awards, including the Lotus Leadership Award, she was named among Apolitical’s 100 Most Influential People in Gender Policy. She also serves on Meta’s Global Advisory Council, the Advertising Standards Council of India, and was previously member of the Trust and Safety Council of Teleperformance and Twitter advocating for safe, respectful online spaces.

name: George Kalu
bio: George Kalu is the Capacity Development Manager at Moxii Africa and a child participation expert with more than 20 years of experience in children’s rights, media, training and programme development. He has trained journalists and child-rights organisations on ethical and meaningful engagement with children and has promoted child-rights programming across child-focused projects. George also supports Moxii Africa’s child online safety work and is currently involved in developing Right Click Africa, an Africa-focused, rights-based media and information literacy curriculum designed to promote and advance digital citizenship among children from birth to 18 years.

name: Gerard Mukhia
bio:
Gerard Mukhia has spent almost a decade at Rescue Foundation, one of India's longest-running anti-trafficking organisations, working across communications, rehabilitation and frontline operations. He has taken part directly in rescue operations, and brings that ground-level view to how the organisation documents and communicates its work.

During the COVID-19 lockdowns, Gerard started the Ekatra project, which trains survivors in shelter homes to become trainers and teachers for their peers. Ekatra is now fully survivor-led.

Gerard also consults with other anti-trafficking organisations, on communications, reporting and programme storytelling. His work focuses on turning frontline experience into evidence that funders, platforms and policymakers can act on.

name: Hasina Kharbhih
designation: FounderHead of Strategic Partnership, Impulse NGO Network
organisation: Impulse NGO Network/ Impulse Social Enterprises
bio:
Hasina Kharbhih | Aspen Fellow /Ashoka Fellow/ Fullbright Scholar
Her work stands on two pillars:  Impulse NGO Network  conceptualized in 1987 a significant force that helps prevent unsafe migration, climate refugees which often leads to human trafficking , the second pillar is Impulse Social Enterprises, promote resilience market to indigenous  artisans and create sustainable economic upliftment.Hasina developed the Impulse Model, an global award Innovation from GDN under JSDF of the World Bank  , a single window approach and  comprehensive strategy in addressing unsafe migration and human trafficking globally.
She has received numerous recognitions, among a few , recipient of 2007- Rising Talent Award from the Women’s Forum for the Economy and Society, France - 2013 International Visitor Leadership Program Gold Star US State Department 2018 Asia Iclif Leadership Energy Award at LESA a leader with intrinsic strength ,that Iclif call Personal Leadership Energy ,a combination of deeply held values and a clear sense of purpose Iclif  Leadership and Governance Centre created by Central Bank of  Malaysia.2019 Mother Teresa Award for Social Justice 2019 from Harmony Foundation for relentless and passionate work and ongoing efforts towards freeing the world from Modern Day Slavery practices, 2019  Listed in Celebrating Changemaker Hers How Women Social Entrepreneur Lead and Innovate ,5000 women Entrepreneurs was Review and 4 Innovation of Leadership was selected. Her leadership style was listed in the recent book as scaling deep, scaling up and scaling out. Recipient  of Women Transforming India Awards (WTI) among the 75 women from across the country who have transformed India and celebrates the dynamic efforts of women by sharing their exemplary stories and exceptional work marking 75 years of Indian independence, by  National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog Government of India .2023 As Aspen Fellow Global Leadership, winner of Global Inclusive Growth Spark Grant collaboration of Mastercard Centre, in addressing system issues across a range of topics including financial security, uplift collaborative efforts.

name: Himadri Sarkar
bio: Himadri Sarkar is Chief Solutions Officer at TP, with more than twenty-five years designing large-scale operational and AI transformation for Fortune 500 organizations. A Lean Six Sigma Master Black Belt, a certified Project Management Professional and an MBA in Finance, he works at the seam between policy and the people it affects. He writes and speaks regularly on the applications of AI in operations and on the discipline of turning strategy into measurable outcomes. His work sits at the seam between policy and the people it affects.

name: Jc Le Toquin
bio:
Jc Le Toquin has a track record in establishing multistakeholder initiatives that strengthen digital safety and security through information sharing, policies and technology solutions, from the Trust & Safety Forum in Lille, France since 2022 to the Trust & Safety Festival, and in particular the annual Trust & Safety India Festival (TASI) in New Delhi since 2025..
A former president of INHOPE, the global network of frontline services against child sexual abuse material online, he co-founded Survivors & Technology Solving Image-Based Sexual Abuse (STISA). STISA works to equip survivor support helplines with the technology, resources, and connections they need to help adult survivors secure the removal of non-consensual intimate images and prevent further revictimisation. 
He is a former Director of the Digital Crimes Unit at Microsoft Europe Middle East & Africa.

name: Ji-yeon Lee
designation: Professor of Counseling and UX Psychology; Director, Human-Centered Digital Safety Lab
bio: Ji-yeon Lee, Ph.D., is a Professor of Counseling and UX Psychology at Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, Seoul, and Director of its Human-Centered Digital Safety Lab. As a licensed psychologist (New York, USA), she brings clinical expertise into user safety research, putting Safety by Design into practice through psychological theory. Her work includes applying trauma-informed user journeys to platform reporting systems so that seeking help protects rather than retraumatises, examining how awareness of online harms reshapes women's social media behaviour even without direct victimisation, and drawing on attachment theory to surface user safety questions in human-AI interaction. She serves on Meta's expert advisory committee on user safety, and works with UN Women as a consultant on its Digital Allies Programme, addressing technology-facilitated gender-based violence across the Asia-Pacific region.

name: Jyoti Vadehra
bio: Jyoti Vadehra is the Lead Digital Trust and Safety, CSR and founding secretariat of the Alliance for Cyber Trust and Safety (ACTS). A strategic expert in the field, she specializes in online safety and wellbeing, and the design and execution of large-scale online safety projects. Jyoti spearheaded the formation of the ACTS alliance and is dedicated to fostering a safer digital ecosystem at the nexus of Gen AI, child safety and wellbeing, gender equality, and sustainable development. Her experience includes significant contributions to policy advocacy, and she is the first Indian representative on Meta’s Board of Global Women’s Safety Expert Advisors.

name: Kartikeya Mitra
bio: Kartikeya is a veteran Trust & Safety leader with over 20 years of experience driving large-scale operations across EMEA, MENA, and APAC to combat fraud, protect platform integrity, and advance regulatory compliance. At Google, he spearheaded DigiKavach, the flagship India-first initiative to combat financial fraud in partnership with key regulatory bodies. A seasoned global people manager, he leads Google’s India Trust & Safety operations in India across four sites, stewarding a high-performance team of 100+ professionals. Kartikeya bridges advanced technology, operational excellence, and public policy to counter emerging digital harms at scale.

name: Keemin Ngiam
bio: Keemin is the Vice-President of Partnerships & Strategic Projects at k-ID, a startup providing privacy-preserving age compliance infrastructure for online services and platforms. A lawyer by training, he spent ten years practicing with Latham & Watkins in the US and Asia. Thereafter he was part of Netflix's founding team in APAC where he helped grow the business across India, Korea, and Southeast Asia. He then spent several years in the video games industry at a large global publisher before joining k-ID. Keemin sits on the board of International Justice Mission (Singapore), a non-profit dedicated to eradicating human trafficking and protecting the poor through the rule of law.

name: Khushi Panda
bio:
Khushi is a Communications and Impact Associate at Rescue Foundation, one of India's longest-running anti-trafficking organisations, where she works to strengthen the systems that support survivors of trafficking. She joined as a volunteer and now works across communications, stakeholder engagement, fundraising, volunteer engagement, and the design and implementation of survivor-centred initiatives across the organisation's shelter homes. Her work combines on-ground experience with a focus on improving outcomes for survivors. 

Khushi holds a BSc in Psychological and Behavioural Science from the London School of Economics and Political Science, where her interdisciplinary work explored gender-based violence in India, public policy, behavioural science, data science and the social implications of emerging technologies. She is particularly interested in how technology, behaviour and institutional systems can be designed to advance safety, gender equity and survivor-centred responses to violence.

name: Kunal Majumder
bio:
Kunāl Majumder is a journalist and press freedom advocate serving as CPJ’s Asia-Pacific Program Coordinator, where he leads advocacy and engagement on journalist safety and press freedom across the region. A journalist since 2006, he has held editorial leadership roles at Tehelka, Rajasthan Patrika, and The Indian Express, and has received the Statesman Award for Rural Reporting and the UNFPA-Laadli Award for Gender Sensitivity.

His work on press freedom and journalist safety has earned international recognition, including a Knight-Wallace Fellowship at the University of Michigan (2024–25), where he researched press freedom and public policy and explored the use of AI and augmented reality (AR) in journalist safety training, and selection for the European Union Visitors’ Programme in 2022. He has also taught journalism at Jamia Millia Islamia’s AJK Mass Communication Research Centre and the University of Michigan’s English Department as a guest faculty member, and delivered the 2025 TEDxUofM talk on the vital role of press freedom in protecting fundamental rights.

A graduate of Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi, and Sciences Po, Paris, Kunāl holds an MA in Journalism and a BA (Honours) in English Literature, Political Science, and History. He speaks English, Bengali, and Hindi. Since 2013, he has served as a pro bono advisor to Impulse NGO Network’s Model Press Lab, contributing to its work on human rights and social justice.

name: Laura Higgins
designation: Senior Director of Community Safety & Civility
bio:
Laura Higgins is Senior Director of Community Safety and Civility at Roblox and has years of experience building safeguarding, online safety and civility programs. Roblox’s digital civility initiative is focused on empowering people to navigate Roblox and the online world with confidence, in partnership with the world’s leading safety and child focused organizations.


In her previous role with the UK Safer Internet Centre, Laura founded several award-winning helpline services, and worked with the biggest names in tech. She has spoken on digital safety topics across the globe and regularly appears in the media sharing her expertise with industry experts, parents and kids.

name: Lisa Morrison
designation: Membership Development and Engagement Manager, APAC
bio:
Lisa Morrison leads membership development and engagement across the Asia-Pacific region for the Tech Coalition (TC), bringing technology companies together to strengthen the industry’s collective response to online child sexual exploitation and abuse.
Before joining the TC, Lisa worked at Meta, where she held roles spanning content policy and trust and safety, including managing responses to complex, high-risk incidents. She previously spent more than a decade working in human rights and humanitarian response with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees across Asia, Africa and Latin America.
Based in Singapore, Lisa is particularly focused on ensuring that global child-safety initiatives reflect the diverse realities, risks and capabilities of the APAC region, and on fostering meaningful collaboration between industry, civil society, governments and law enforcement.

name: Lucy Thomas
bio:
Lucy Thomas OAM is cofounder and CEO of PROJECT ROCKIT, Australia’s youth-driven movement working to create kinder, safer and more inclusive communities. Lucy launched PROJECT ROCKIT with their sister Rosie straight out of high school and has spent the past two decades working alongside young people to challenge bullying, amplify youth voice and shape the culture around them. Through its youth-driven school programs, PROJECT ROCKIT has directly impacted more than 1 million school students and supported more than 150 young people into career-starting employment in the social impact sector.

Lucy is also a trusted voice in online safety, serving on global Safety Advisory Boards for Meta, Snapchat, Spotify and Roblox, where they bring young people’s perspectives into conversations about technology and online safety. A passionate speaker and facilitator, Lucy brings together youth voice, creativity and advocacy to explore how we can build better ways of being together – online and off.

Lucy is an Obama Leader and Westpac Social Change Fellow, and was awarded a Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) for their service to youth and the prevention of bullying.

name: M. C. Rasmin
bio: Dr. M. C. Rasmin is a researcher and practitioner specialising in child online safety, digital mental health, internet psychology, and media literacy. His work focuses on preventing online child sexual exploitation, promoting digital wellbeing, and advancing evidence-based policies and interventions that protect children in the digital environment. He has led numerous national and international initiatives on digital rights, child protection, and media literacy while working closely with governments, international organisations, and civil society partners. His research continues to explore the relationship between technology, child development, and mental wellbeing.

name: Madelaine Coelho
bio: Madelaine Coelho is a PhD Candidate in the University of Toronto’s Department of Sociology. Her research explores resources available for survivors of technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV) pan-India and, more broadly, Indian responses to gender-based violence in a digital world. This research has been supported through a Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship, Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) research grants, and a Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society Graduate Fellowship. With a background in both computer science and sociology, Madelaine is passionate about interdisciplinary solutions to complex problems surrounding gender, violence, and technology.

name: Madeline Shepherd
bio:
Madeline Shepherd (she/her) is Director of Public Policy, Digital Safety at Microsoft, where she leads the company's global policy strategy on online safety, child protection, and responsible technology governance. Her work focuses on shaping practical, evidence-based approaches to digital safety that support innovation while protecting users, particularly children and young people.

A recognised leader in digital safety policy, Madeline works extensively with governments, regulators, international organisations, and industry stakeholders to advance policy solutions on issues such as age assurance, online harms, non-consensual intimate imagery, AI safety, and safety-by-design. She is particularly passionate about how technology, policy, and education can work together to support the trusted adults who play a critical role in children's online lives.

name: Margaret Gichanga
bio: Dr Margaret Gichanga is a fundraising and research consultant to Kutunga, which advances safety-by-design for children's digital products across Africa through the A-CODES Fellowship, the Kutunga Sandbox, and the Kutunga Seal certification, built on the WATOTO framework's ten African-grounded standards. She holds a PhD in Business and Management and a Master's in International Relations, and has led policy research and engaged directly with government and civil society stakeholders throughout her career. She currently leads research design for a multi-country study on how African parents and children experience data practices and safety mechanisms in the digital products their children use daily.

name: Nandini Chatterjee Singh
designation: Professor, Dept. of Psychology and Cognitive Science
bio: Leading cognitive neuroscientist and science-policy education researcher. Established track record of combining innovative thinking with scientific evidence and research to develop, design and implement original solutions. Collaborates with civil society, social institutions, policy makers and government bodies to translate research from the laboratory to the real world. Compassionate leader, values empathy, out of the box thinking, replicable evidence, inclusion and attention to detail.

name: Nina Bual
bio:
Nina Bual is the co-founder  and Managing Director of Cyberlite, a leading social enterprise dedicated to promoting sustainable and equitable cyber safety and generative AI education across the Asia-Pacific region, with offices in Singapore and India. Cyberlite designs and implements comprehensive programs for child online safety and cyber resilience building in diverse communities, with an innovative approach to localisation that aligns with international policies and curricula. 

Cyberlite is also the recipient of the Digital for Life Catalyst award by Singapore’s President Shanmugaratnam for its significant contributions to child online safety education.

Nina is a regular speaker at international events organised by the ASEAN-Singapore Cybersecurity Centre of Excellence (ASCCE), ECPAT, and the GFCE.

name: Omari Rodney
bio:
Omari Rodney is the Chief Product Engineer at Yoti, specialising in online safety, privacy technologies, and age assurance. With over 10 years experience in the industry, Omari has contributed to the development and implementation of solutions that prioritise user empowerment and privacy. Omari has spoken at the Global Age Assurance Summit and Yoti’s regulatory roundtables.

With a BEng in software engineering and a Msc in Photonic Networks, Omari has over 15 years of experience developing mission critical systems. At Yoti, Omari looks after the development of safety products and responsible use of data across a range of sectors.

Outside of Yoti Omari, is an advisor to the social mobility charity The 93% Club.

name: Pragya Misra
designation: Head of Strategy & Global Affairs, India, OpenAI
bio:
At OpenAI, Pragya leads Strategy & Global Affairs for India, one of the world’s most transformative AI markets. She works across product, policy, partnerships, and GTM to ensure we present one OpenAI story that aligns our mission with India’s priorities.

Before OpenAI, Pragya spearheaded Public Affairs at Truecaller, the leading caller identification app. Pragya joined Truecaller from WhatsApp, where she was one of their first hires in India, managing Communications and driving reputation and advocacy efforts. She holds a Master of Business Administration (MBA) from the International Management Institute, and a Bachelor's degree in Commerce from Delhi University.

name: Rob Lewington
designation: SVP | Head of Global Trust & Safety
bio: Rob Lewington is a Trust & Safety leader with nearly two decades of experience steering platform safety, operational resilience, and risk mitigation. Having previously spearheaded Trust & Safety operations for global technology giants including Amazon and Sony, he now leads Teleperformance’s global Trust & Safety portfolio. In this role, he oversees approximately 50,000 safety professionals delivering integrity, compliance, and moderation solutions across 70+ client environments worldwide.  He is currently driving TP's AI-driven transformation of Trust & Safety operations, advancing human-in-the-loop and human-on-the-loop governance at scale.

name: S. Krishnan
bio: S. Krishnan is the Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India. As a member of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) since 1989, he has extensive experience across a range of assignments with the Government of Tamil Nadu, the Government of India, and the International Monetary Fund (IMF). His expertise includes public finance, policymaking, and governance.

name: Satviki Varma
bio:
Satviki Varma is a development professional with extensive experience leading multi-sectoral programmes across health, gender, adolescent wellbeing and digital safety in India and globally. She currently leads programmes at Girl Effect India, where she has been closely involved in the organisation’s work to address technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV) through research, youth engagement, school-based interventions, digital campaigns and multi-stakeholder partnerships.

Her work includes leading the development and scale-up of Tipi Tipi Talk, a school-based digital safety programme, and contributing to Girl Effect’s wider India vs Tech Hinsa initiative, which brings together behaviour change, storytelling, education and systems-level engagement to prevent and respond to online gender-based violence.

Previously, Satviki has worked with the Children’s Investment Fund Foundation (CIFF), Aga Khan Foundation, John Snow India (JSI), and the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) in Geneva. Her experience spans programme strategy, human-centred design and locally led development, including initiatives reaching over 150,000 households across 11 states. A former journalist, she brings together systems thinking and storytelling to drive social change and build safer, more equitable environments for young people.

name: Siddharth P
bio: Siddharth Pillai is Co-Founder and Co- Director of RATI Foundation, with over 15 years of experience across digital safety, research and advocacy in the nonprofit sector. At RATI, he leads the organisation’s online safety strategy and has co-created initiatives including Meri Trustline - a national helpline supporting people facing online abuse and the Ideal Internet research series examining children’s experiences of the digital world. His work has included developing child online safety frameworks with the Ministry of Women & Child Development, UNESCO Asia-Pacific and other national and international bodies.

name: Smriti Irani
bio:
Smriti Zubin Irani is a prominent politician and a former TV star. She left a lucrative career to join politics over two decades ago and has been a Cabinet minister from 2014-24, a three-time Member of Parliament and has held various posts in BJP.

She created history in 2019 by defeating the then-president of Congress from Amethi, a seat seen as nearly impossible to win by a non-Congress politician.

Mrs. Irani earlier represented Gujarat in the Upper House, Rajya Sabha (2011-2017), and was re-elected from Gujarat in 2017.
Her past ministerial portfolios include Ministry of Women & Child Development (2019-24), Ministry of Minority Affairs (2022-24) — The first non-Muslim to hold the position, Ministry of Human Resource Development (2014-16), Ministry of Information & Broadcasting (2017-18), and Ministry of Textiles (2016-21).

She was India’s youngest Cabinet Minister in Modi 1.0 & 2.0 and the first woman to hold office as Union Minister for HRD & Textiles.

In the 126th Assembly of Inter-Parliamentary Union, she was unanimously elected as a Member representing the Asia Pacific Region to the Task Force responsible for the 1st ever Committee for Young Parliamentarians in the IPU. At the same Assembly, Mrs. Irani was also unanimously elected by Member Nations as Rapporteur for the Standing Committee on Sustainable Development, Finance & Trade. The World Economic Forum named her as the Young Global Leader from India for the year 2015. She also served as the USAID Goodwill Ambassador to India for the WHO-ORS programme.

She has served in the BJP in various posts such as National Vice President, National President of Women's Wing, Vice President of Maharashtra Youth Wing, National Secretary (twice), 5-term Member of the National Executive, Maharashtra State Secretary & has significantly and successfully pursued Permanent Commission for Women in the Indian Army. She also launched 'Saksham'- the 1st ever Vision Document released by any political organization in India to uplift the Differently-abled in India.

Besides being an active social & political activist, she has had a successful career as a Media Professional for over 2 decades starting from 1994. She has worked across different fields of media right from creating content for news & entertainment Television networks to acting in over 22 television series, 2 films, and 5 theatre projects in 4 Indian languages. Apart from her contributions as an actor, her work in television networks ranged from direction, scriptwriting to production. She has also contributed as a columnist to 2 national dailies.

name: Snigdha Bhardwaj
designation: Director and Global Head of Generative AI, Trust & Safety, Google
bio:
Name: Snigdha Bhardwaj

Title: Director and Global Head of Generative AI, Trust & Safety, Google

Bio: A transformational leader with a 20+ years of experience and strong background in Trust and Safety, currently driving Generative AI testing and enforcement strategy for consumer products in Google. 

Snigdha has been instrumental in setting the framework and direction for key & novel Google launches, including Gemini, Search launches like AIO & AIM, Labs launches like NotebookLM and AI Studios launches, collaborating directly with the Office of the CEO and multiple cross-functional senior leaders. Snigdha's expertise includes developing robust strategies for content and actor-based abuse in Generative AI, with a focus on trust & info quality. Also championing key strategic priorities including implementation & resource allocation for Generative AI launches, advocating for xT&S resourcing to SVPs, and effectively coordinating across multiple organizations to ensure successful pre and post launch support. As a subject matter expert on intelligence and risk related to Generative AI, Snigdha has shared knowledge through numerous tech talks and authored/contributed to extensive documentation, including several senior exec level presentations and external engagements.

Prior to the Generative AI era, Snigdha led various cross functional and complex programs for Google Search overseeing the globally distributed 50+ FTE teams delivery for policy implementation and  enforcement efforts. This included a launch of 100+ features across Search, supporting the automated process development, working with ENG and product, Legal, PR etc to find solutions to the user facing issues, classifier development, intel investigations etc.

Warmest Regards,

name: Sophie Mortimer
bio:
Sophie Mortimer is Head of Support Services at SWGfL, responsible for the UK Revenge Porn Helpline, the only dedicated service providing specialist support to adults affected by intimate image abuse in the UK. Under her leadership, the Helpline has become an essential resource, offering expert guidance to those navigating the challenges of this deeply personal form of online harm. Sophie also plays a pivotal role in StopNCII.org, a global platform enabling individuals to protect their private images across the world from unauthorised sharing across partner platforms.
A passionate advocate for online safety and survivor support, Sophie speaks at events in the UK and internationally, promoting cross-border collaboration as vital to addressing the global nature of online abuse. Her work spans survivor advocacy, public awareness, and policy influence, alongside championing innovative technological solutions. Sophie's dedication to fostering partnerships and raising awareness makes her a leading figure in the fight against tech-facilitated gender-based violence and a prominent voice for change.

name: Triveni Acharya
bio:
Triveni Acharya is the President and CEO of Rescue Foundation, one of India's leading anti-human-trafficking organizations, based in Mumbai. Over three decades, her work has helped rescue and rehabilitate thousands of women and girls trafficked into forced prostitution across India, with the organization's reach extending to repatriations across South Asia and beyond.

A former journalist, Acharya's mission began in 1993 when a reporting assignment in Mumbai's Kamathipura red-light district led her into a brothel where she found girls being held against their will. Alongside her husband, Balkrishna Acharya, she carried out her first rescue soon after. In 2000, the couple founded Rescue Foundation. Following her husband's death in 2005, Acharya took over full leadership of the organization.

Under her direction, Rescue Foundation has rescued more than 7,000 women and girls from forced prostitution through intelligence-led operations conducted with law enforcement. The organization runs four shelter homes — in Mumbai, Boisar, Pune, and Delhi — providing medical care, counseling, education, and vocational training, and has repatriated survivors to Nepal, Bangladesh, Thailand, Uzbekistan, Kenya, and Nigeria.

Acharya's work has been recognized internationally, including the Asia Democracy and Human Rights Award (2010), the Civil Courage Prize (2011), the World of Children Humanitarian Award (2013, 2015), recognition among the President of India's 100 Women Achievers (2016) and last year with the Jamnalal Bajaj Award.

name: Uma Submanian
bio: Uma Subramanian is Co-Founder and Director of RATI Foundation and a social worker with over 15 years of experience in child protection. She co-founded the Aarambh India Initiative, which established India’s first hotline for reporting child sexual abuse material (CSAM), and was recognised with the Presidential National Award for Child Welfare. At RATI, she co-leads organizational strategy across child protection and online safety. Uma is also a master trainer who has trained more than 5,000 stakeholders on various aspects of child protection, including responding to online sexual abuse.

name: Uthara Ganesh
bio:
Uthara Ganesh, Head of Public Policy, APAC, Snap Inc.

Uthara leads Public Policy for Snap Inc. in the APAC region, driving engagement with governments across India, Australia, China, Singapore, Indonesia amongst other markets. She’s previously led policy at Amazon and advised Minister Rajeev Chandrasekhar. Her career spans roles at CPR, UNAIDS, and GIZ, and she is a former LAMP Fellow.

name: Vaibhav Pulekar
organisation: TUV SUD South Asia Pvt Ltd
bio:

name: Yoel Roth
designation: SVP, Head of Trust and Safety
bio:
Yoel Roth is a trust and safety practitioner and researcher. He is the Senior Vice President of Trust & Safety at Match Group, the parent company of Tinder, Hinge, and dozens of dating apps used by millions of people worldwide. He is also a Non-Resident Scholar at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, where his research, teaching, and writing focus on trustworthy governance approaches for social media, AI, and other emerging technologies.

Previously, Yoel was the Head of Trust & Safety at Twitter. For more than 7 years, he helped build and lead the teams responsible for Twitter’s content moderation, integrity, and election security efforts.

Yoel received his PhD from the Annenberg School for Communication at the University of Pennsylvania. His research examined the technical, policy, business, and governance dynamics of app stores, social networking, and online dating.
